about: Domaine Olga Raffault is a family estate in Savigny-en-Véron, in the western corner of the Chinon appellation along the Vienne river. Olga married fellow grower Pierre Raffault in 1931. After his death in 1947 she kept the domaine going with the help of Ernest Zenninger, a former German prisoner of war who stayed on as winemaker. Her granddaughter Sylvie Raffault now runs the estate with her husband Éric de la Vigerie and their son Arnaud: about 25 hectares, certified organic since 2013.

Les Picasses is the estate’s flagship and a benchmark of Chinon terroir. The Cabernet Franc vines, more than fifty years old, grow on a fairly steep, south-facing slope on the north bank of the Vienne, in clay over chalky tuffeau limestone. The grapes are picked by hand and fermented as whole berries for 25 to 30 days in stainless steel. The wine then ages for years in large, old foudres, sometimes of local chestnut, and is released about four years after the harvest.

Vinous’s Rebecca Gibb called the 2020, from a warm year, a ripe Chinon, with a concentrated, silky middle, chalky tannins, fresh acidity and raspberry fruit. Expect a perfumed red with plum, wild blackberry and flowers, firm tannins and a peppery finish. Les Picasses has a long record of ageing for decades, and the estate’s late release means it is already starting to open when it reaches the table.
